body:
Full-codebase review, cross-client finding. Verified, including the comparison behaviour in both languages.

Category canonical casing breaks ties differently on the two clients. Web: `count === bestCount && casing.localeCompare(best) < 0`. Android: `count == bestCount && casing < best` (UTF-16 code units). With one item "Obst" and one "obst" and no category_order entry, `"obst".localeCompare("Obst")` is -1 so the web labels the bucket **obst**, while `"Obst" < "obst"` is true in Kotlin so Android labels it **Obst**. Both clients offer that name for the "fix casing everywhere" action, so the two clients write different values to the same shared list. The autocomplete order diverges the same way (`localeCompare` vs `.sorted()`): for "Äpfel"/"Bananen" web puts Ä first, Android B first.

The repo already solved this class of problem once: `shared-test-cases/name-order.json` says ordering must never be locale-aware, and `nameOrder.ts` has `byCodeUnits` for exactly this. Both clients' own tests dodge the tie by using unequal counts.

Fix direction: use the shared code-unit comparison on both sides, and add a `category-canon` group to shared-test-cases.
title: Cross-client: category canonical casing and autocomplete order diverge between the clients
